findings.what: 0 is refused with '<option> must be a whole number of milliseconds', though 0 is a whole number (the rule broken is 'at least 1'; I3 of step 04b; the shape of L3, which I should have found in pass 1 with L3, AP-014). A value of 2^31 or more is accepted, but Node keeps no timer that long: it sets it to 1 ms with a TimeoutOverflowWarning. Measured (bigtimeout.mjs): startTimeoutMs 2^31 ends the start after 26 ms with 'fake did not print its link in 2147483648 ms; it was killed'. stopTimeoutMs 2^31 makes a stand that exits 0 on SIGTERM end as STAND_STOP_TIMEOUT 'did not stop in 2147483648 ms after SIGTERM; it was killed'. So a bad option spawns a process, kills it, and reports a false time (I4 (a) of SECURITY-REVIEWER, given to REVIEWER). No real caller gives such values, hence Low.
findings.fix: Refuse a timeout outside 1…2147483647 with USAGE and name the range in the message ('must be a whole number of milliseconds from 1 to 2147483647'); say 'without NUL' for cwd as for args and env.

Node passes NODE_V8_COVERAGE on even when the starter gives a short environment; it is a switch of the developer's shell when coverage is on. The starter itself passes nothing else, so the texts are true of the starter but not of what the child gets (I5 of step 04b; F1 and I3 of step 03). E2S-05 allows the first name, and TEST-DESIGNER has been told about the second (I3 of step 03).

issues.text: decisions/0109, the corrected O13: the facts of my trial are recorded truly, and 'cannot be forced with Node alone' holds for a stand started the real way. The reason given, '(Node reaps its children)', is not accurate. A Node parent whose event loop is blocked does not reap: E2K-62 keeps a killed child unreaped exactly that way. The real reason is the process group. Node has no call that moves a process into another group or out of its own (process.setsid, setpgid, setpgrp are undefined; spawn knows only detached, which makes a new group). So every member of the stand's group descends from the leader inside the group, its parent dies with the group SIGKILL, and the system's first process reaps the orphan. (A fake child given through deps.spawn could imitate the case; O13 already declines test-only hooks.) Proposal for ORCH: reword the parenthesis, for example '(no Node call moves a process out of its process group, so the parent of every member dies with the group's SIGKILL and the system reaps the orphan)'. Linux not measured. The record is ORCH's (quality-bar §6 item 7); nothing in the code depends on it.

The design texts now lag behind the README and the code (I4 of step 04b, AP-005, AP-077): section 10 item 3 of docs/design/REQ-105-e2e-picker.md is the source text of README line 844 and lacks the two inserted clauses (and L6 if taken); section 4.1 lacks the reading of O14; section 15 row R2 says the starter keeps the real home folder from REQ-106's stand, which is false (O15). For DOC-UPDATER at step 10, with README line 844 and section 10 item 3 in the same edit. L5 is a small CODE-FIXER edit if ORCH wants it before the tests; otherwise it is recorded for the report.

New behaviour to cover (through ORCH): (a) M1: a readyPattern whose one group takes no part (optional, or in the other alternative) gives URL_REFUSED with '[undefined]'; afterwards the group is gone, nothing is registered and there is no marker. (b) L1: a deps.spawn that returns a child with no pid and no pipes, and emits error EMFILE on the next tick, gives STAND_START_FAILED with no crash and no marker. A deps.spawn fake that returns a child with a pid must give real streams (a PassThrough), because only the stream is guarded with ?., not its methods. (c) L2: no cleanupError when the body awaited the failing stop(). (d) I4: a frozen body error with a failing stop is rethrown as the same object; a body that throws null rejects with null. (e) L3: the message 'must be a string without NUL', with the value absent. (f) E2S-05: NODE_V8_COVERAGE when the parent has it (I3 of step 03). My trials in <scratch>/e2e105r/trials/ (outcomes.mjs, withstand2.mjs, envtruth.mjs, bigtimeout.mjs) may be reused.
